amendments.because: Narrowed under the owner's Harm 1-2 rule: fixes already stop hard at the commit hook, and keying id-less Jest or Vitest failures by test name is a follow-up; both scored Gain 2, Harm 1
amendments.done_when: When two rounds in a row leave the same failing test or finding, or the change grows past its size limit, Forge stops the item and prints a ready-to-ask question naming the item, what is stuck and what the worker tried, with the choices: switch this item to the other tool, keep the same tool for one more round, or narrow or split; the owner's choice is recorded and the next round follows it

done_when: When two rounds in a row leave the same failing test (by its test id; for runners without ids, by its failure lines) or the same finding, or a story part grows past its size limit, Forge stops the item and prints a ready-to-ask question naming the item, what is stuck and what the worker tried, with the choices: switch this item to the other tool, keep the same tool for one more round, or narrow or split; the owner's choice is recorded and the next round follows it. A fix past its five-code-file limit keeps the commit hook's existing refusal.

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The new size-question path applies only when the item name contains `/`, so it covers story parts but not fixes. A fix that grows beyond its five-code-file limit is instead refused by the existing pre-commit rule in `src/forge/githooks.py:213-215`, with no ready-to-ask question or recorded choice among switch, same, narrow and split. The named size proof exercises only a story part.
findings.title: Not done: oversized fixes never produce the required owner question

findings.body: Raise: Not done. For Jest or Vitest output without a `FAILED ...::...` identifier, the failure key includes the first 200 characters of every matching failure line. If a worker changes an implementation but leaves the same test failing with a different `AssertionError` value, that key changes and the consecutive-round count resets. Forge keeps sending the item back instead of asking the owner. The named Jest proof varies only the duration, which this line removes.
findings.title: Not done: changed assertion text hides a repeated failing test

stop.reason: Owner rule for Harm 1-2: findings 1-3 are fixed in commit fa1b2eedc; findings 4 (no-commit wording) and 5 (question waits for a lane slot) are Gain 2, lived with, with notes in the proof list

why: When a worker can't fix a problem or keeps making the change bigger, Forge sends it back round after round and nobody is told
